title: Tompkins and Webster's school escapades and hearing Lunceford at the Parlor
summary: Webster and Tompkins joined Lunceford in summers; Durham heard the band at the Parlor, found it a show band, and joined at $35 a week.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah, but he got in so much trouble all the time. They suspended him the last year because he went -- we would always go down to the school at night and get into the laboratory and get whisky and stuff for the band.

And he got (inaudible) all drunk and he knocked over something and started a fire. He got burned, got burned in there, and they had to get him out. And they put him out of the school because he'd been doing it all along. But they'd go to school, and as soon as school was out, they'd tear to Buffalo and join Lunceford's band. They'd say, Lunceford, we got a trombone man with us.
And, quite naturally, when they played anything, we had our own routines.

We could get in the band and the brass would take over a couple of choruses. And that's how I got in Lunceford's band. He was playing the Parlor, and I went down and heard the band, I thought the band was fantastic, it was a show band.
So I said, I think I'll come in, because Lunceford was paying $35 a week or something like
